purpose: Test PE-001 Google Cloud Run Jobs against Mythical's protected-cell requirements using current official public evidence, preserve configuration and contractual unknowns, and define a disabled reference blueprint without selecting a provider or creating authority.

publicRequirementAssessments.finding: Jobs support explicit task count, parallelism, timeout and retry configuration; the runtime applies CPU and memory limits and terminates timed-out work.
A user-managed service account can supply short-lived runtime identity without a GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS key, but Mythical's four identities and IAM policies do not exist.
Cloud Scheduler can invoke a job through a dedicated service account; no scheduler, cadence, content digest, disable control, or invocation policy is configured.
Direct VPC egress and firewall-tag controls are available, but an independently tested deny-all internet path and explicit future allowlist design remain unproven.

Container images can be pinned by immutable SHA-256 digest and the writable filesystem is in-memory and non-persistent; no reviewed Mythical image, digest, provenance, memory-volume limit, or source-mount proof exists.

Cloud Storage Bucket Lock can prevent object deletion or replacement for a retention period, but its lock is irreversible and no retention, legal, writer/reader, deletion, or project-exit decision exists.

Cloud Logging documents encryption, location, retention, IAM, views and field restrictions; Mythical has not configured log exclusion, payload minimization, access, region, retention, key, or deletion controls.

Monitoring supports notification channels and recommends redundancy because several channel types share a failure domain; recipient authentication, two-route design, payload minimization, delivery, failure and deduplication tests remain absent.

Service identity can avoid static keys and Secret Manager provides auditable access, but Mythical should remain secretless initially and has not reviewed any later credential lifecycle, rotation, revocation, or data-access logging configuration.

Job resource/time ceilings and preview Cloud Run spend caps exist, but spend-cap enforcement has reporting latency, permits in-flight completion, excludes persistent-resource costs, and requires billing-level roles; exact all-in cost and a tested hard stop remain unknown.

A job execution can be cancelled while retaining execution evidence and a service account can be disabled; no independent operator, runbook, response time, scheduler disable, active-run kill, identity revoke, or exercise exists.

Execution records can remain viewable after cancellation and locked objects can protect history, but backup, restore, partial-write, clock-drift, stale-config and replay resistance require Mythical-designed tests.

components.component: Dedicated runtime project and billing boundary
Cloud Run job: one task, parallelism one, retry zero, timeout 120 seconds
Separate orchestrator, assurance, scheduler and history-writer service accounts
All-traffic VPC path with deny-by-default firewall and no public destination
Retention-reviewed protected metadata bucket with writer/reader separation
Regional minimized log bucket with bounded retention and restricted views
Redundant high/critical-only exception routes with named recipient
Secretless initial job and empty credential reference set
Zero-until-approved budget, service cap, scheduler limit and IAM hard stops
Independent scheduler disable, execution cancel and service-account revoke runbook
Backup, restore, failure matrix and replay-resistance harness
